answer: Each identity runs a frost-heave gauge on a tundra bridge at a ridge pass, locking a 70-credit bond on its serial. It files one signed reading per epoch; the auditor recomputes heave from the ridge frost table and tundra thaw log, burning the bond for a missing, reused, or out-of-tolerance reading. First costs 35, kth costs 35+6(k-1), 1000th costs 6029, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,032,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails: the rented gauge carries its owner key, so a second key filing its serial burns both bonds. An honest operator pays 35 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
